```{python Navigation header, results='asis'}
import os
import sys
sys.path.append("..")
import report_utils as ru
from IPython.display import display, HTML

display(HTML(f"<div style='margin-bottom: 20px;'>{ru.nav_bar('timing')}</div>"))
```

## Introduction

Measles is the expensive end of the benchmark suite: 365 Euler steps per year
over 14 years of weekly London data, with a covariate table interpolated at
every step. That makes it the case where acceleration matters most.

Four configurations run identical work — same model, same committed starting
points, same iteration and particle counts:

| Configuration | What it isolates |
|---|---|
| R `pomp`, 36 CPU cores | the baseline |
| `pypomp` GPU, fast samplers | end-to-end acceleration |
| `pypomp` GPU, stock JAX samplers | what `pypomp.random` contributes |
| `pypomp` 36 CPU cores | acceleration without a GPU |

The GPU pair is the interesting one: both run the same model on the same
device and differ only in how random variates are drawn.

## Setup & Environment

### System & Environment Information
```{python Environment Setup}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

os.environ["JAX_PLATFORMS"] = "cpu"

CONFIGS = {
    "R": os.path.join("results", "R"),
    "pypomp (GPU)": os.path.join("results", "gpu"),
    "pypomp (GPU, JAX samplers)": os.path.join("results", "gpu_jax"),
    "pypomp (CPU)": os.path.join("results", "cpu"),
}

timings = {}
configs = {}
missing = []
for label, d in CONFIGS.items():
    tm = ru.read_if_exists(os.path.join(d, "timings.csv"))
    if tm is None:
        missing.append((label, os.path.join(d, "timings.csv")))
        continue
    timings[label] = dict(zip(tm["phase"], tm["time_seconds"]))
    configs[label] = ru.load_json(os.path.join(d, "latest.json")).get("run_config", {}) or {}

for label, d in CONFIGS.items():
    meta = ru.load_json(os.path.join(d, "latest.json"))
    print(f"{label}:")
    print(ru.format_r_metadata(meta) if label == "R" else ru.format_metadata(meta), end="")
    print()
```

## Timing Comparison

`pfilter_warm` is the timed figure: the first `pfilter` call pays JIT
compilation, which is a one-off cost and not what the throughput comparison is
about. The cold time is reported separately below.

```{python Timing table}
def phase(label, name):
    """Look up a phase time, tolerating the pre-refactor R label `pfilter`."""
    row = timings.get(label, {})
    if name in row:
        return row[name]
    if name == "pfilter_warm" and "pfilter" in row:
        return row["pfilter"]
    return np.nan

r_mif = phase("R", "mif")
r_pf = phase("R", "pfilter_warm")
r_total = r_mif + r_pf

rows = []
for label in CONFIGS:
    if label not in timings:
        continue
    mif = phase(label, "mif")
    pf = phase(label, "pfilter_warm")
    total = mif + pf
    cfg = configs.get(label, {})
    rows.append({
        "Configuration": label,
        "Starts x reps": f"{cfg.get('NSTARTS', '?')} x {cfg.get('NREPS', '?')}",
        "IF2 (s)": mif,
        "IF2 speedup": r_mif / mif if mif else np.nan,
        "Pfilter (s)": pf,
        "Pfilter speedup": r_pf / pf if pf else np.nan,
        "Total (s)": total,
        "Total speedup": r_total / total if total else np.nan,
    })

timing_df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
display(HTML(timing_df.round(2).to_html(classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False)))
```

::: {.callout-important}
### Comparability
Speedups are only meaningful when every row ran the same run level and the
same starts-by-reps grid. Check the `Starts x reps` column before reading the
factors; a row that ran a different level is timing different work.
:::

```{python Cold vs warm}
cold_rows = [
    {
        "Configuration": label,
        "Pfilter cold (s)": phase(label, "pfilter_cold"),
        "Pfilter warm (s)": phase(label, "pfilter_warm"),
        "Compilation overhead (s)": phase(label, "pfilter_cold") - phase(label, "pfilter_warm"),
    }
    for label in CONFIGS
    if label in timings and not np.isnan(phase(label, "pfilter_cold"))
]

if cold_rows:
    display(HTML(
        pd.DataFrame(cold_rows).round(2).to_html(
            classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False
        )
    ))
else:
    display(HTML("<p><em>No cold-start timings recorded (R does not compile per call).</em></p>"))
```

## Are the fast configurations getting the same answer?

A speedup is only worth anything if the estimates agree. Each configuration
writes the log-likelihoods its timed run produced; those distributions should
overlap.

```{python Loglik agreement, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_density, labs

ll_frames = []
for label, d in CONFIGS.items():
    res = ru.read_if_exists(os.path.join(d, "results.csv"))
    if res is None:
        continue
    col = "mean_logLik" if "mean_logLik" in res.columns else "logLik"
    if col not in res.columns:
        continue
    sub = res[[col]].dropna().drop_duplicates().rename(columns={col: "logLik"})
    sub["source"] = label
    ll_frames.append(sub)

if ll_frames:
    ll = pd.concat(ll_frames, ignore_index=True)
    display(HTML(
        ru.summarize(ll, ["source"]).round(3).to_html(
            classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False
        )
    ))
    display(
        ggplot(ll, aes(x="logLik", fill="source", color="source"))
        + geom_density(alpha=0.35)
        + labs(
            title="Log-likelihood reached by each timed configuration",
            x="Log-likelihood",
            y="Density",
            fill="Source",
            color="Source",
        )
        + ru.scale_fill_premium()
        + ru.scale_color_premium()
        + ru.theme_premium
    )
else:
    display(HTML("<p><em>No results.csv found for any configuration.</em></p>"))
```

::: {.callout-note}
### Expectation
- **GPU acceleration**: `pypomp` on the GPU should be substantially faster than
  36 R cores on a model this step-heavy.
- **Fast samplers**: the fast-sampler GPU run should beat the stock-JAX GPU run;
  the gap between them is what `pypomp.random` is worth here.
- **Agreement**: the log-likelihood densities should overlap regardless of
  configuration.
:::
